examples.question_text:
Verify by differentiation and substitution that each function satisfies its differential equation.
(a) $Q=28+36e^{kt}$; $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}=k(Q-28)$.
(b) $N=900-300e^{-kt}$; $\dfrac{dN}{dt}=-k(N-900)$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Differentiate the proposed function:
$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{dQ}{dt}&=36ke^{kt}.\end{aligned}$
Substitute into the right-hand side:
$\begin{aligned}k(Q-28)&=k(28+36e^{kt}-28)\\&=36ke^{kt}.\end{aligned}$
Both sides agree, so the function satisfies the differential equation.
(b) Differentiate the proposed function:
$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{dN}{dt}&=(-300)(-k)e^{-kt}\\&=300ke^{-kt}.\end{aligned}$
Substitute into the right-hand side:
$\begin{aligned}-k(N-900)&=-k(900-300e^{-kt}-900)\\&=300ke^{-kt}.\end{aligned}$
Both sides agree. The negative coefficient and negative exponent produce a positive derivative when $k>0$.

examples.question_text:
A drink cools in a room at $22^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. Its temperature is modelled by $T=22+Ae^{kt}$, where $t$ is measured in minutes. Initially its temperature is $86^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, and after $6$ minutes it is $54^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.
(a) Find $A$ and $k$ in exact form.
(b) Find its temperature after $12$ minutes.
(c) Sketch the temperature against time for $t\ge0$, showing the initial temperature and horizontal asymptote.

A battery charges towards a maximum charge of $100\%$. Initially its charge is $20\%$, and after $4$ minutes it is $60\%$. Its charge is modelled by $Q=P+Ae^{kt}$, where $k<0$ and $t$ is measured in minutes.
(a) Write an expression for $Q(t)$ before determining $k$.
(b) Find $k$ in exact form.
(c) Sketch $Q$ against $t$ for $t\ge0$, labelling the initial charge and asymptote.

Sketch each function for $t\ge0$, showing its initial value and the line $Q=30$. Describe whether it has a limiting value.
(a) $Q=30+10e^{0.2t}$.
(b) $Q=30-10e^{0.2t}$.

The graph of $Q=8+Ae^{kt}$ passes through $(0,12)$ and $(3,40)$.
Find $A$ and $k$ in exact form. State whether the graph approaches a limiting value as $t\to\infty$.
examples.solution_text:
Use the initial point:
$\begin{aligned}12&=8+A\\A&=4.\end{aligned}$
Use the second point:
$\begin{aligned}40&=8+4e^{3k}\\32&=4e^{3k}\\e^{3k}&=8\\3k&=\ln8\\k&=\ln2.\end{aligned}$
Thus $Q=8+4e^{(\ln2)t}$. Since $A>0$ and $k>0$, the curve rises away from $Q=8$ and grows without bound. It has no finite limiting value.

coverage.summary: Authored five examples covering all distinct accepted assessment methods with changed values and booklet-taught working. Graphs cover all four nonzero sign combinations; annotations appear only in solutions. Separate editable prompt and solution fields use inline aligned mathematics, with solution colour supplied by the renderer. Assessments were classified only and remain unchanged. Independent example review and actual rendering verification remain pending.

examples.derivation: For (a), Q'=36ke^{kt} and k(Q-28)=36ke^{kt}. For (b), N'=300ke^{-kt} and -k(N-900)=300ke^{-kt}. Each derivative agrees independently with its substituted right-hand side.

The initial condition gives A=86-22=64. The second observation gives e^{6k}=32/64=1/2, hence k=-ln(2)/6. Therefore T(12)=22+64(1/2)^2=38 degrees Celsius. The plotted expression starts at 86 and decreases towards 22 from above.

The maximum charge gives P=100, and A=20-100=-80. Substituting the second observation gives e^{4k}=(-40)/(-80)=1/2, hence k=-ln(2)/4. The plotted expression starts at 20 and increases towards 100 from below.

The initial values are 40 and 20. The derivatives are respectively 2e^{0.2t} and -2e^{0.2t}, with second derivatives 0.4e^{0.2t} and -0.4e^{0.2t}. The curves therefore steepen upwards and downwards respectively, with no finite limiting value. Both plotted expressions and reference lines agree with these conclusions.

The initial point gives A=12-8=4. The second point gives e^{3k}=(40-8)/4=8, so k=ln(8)/3=ln(2). Thus Q=8+4e^{(ln2)t} grows without bound and has no finite limiting value. A diagram is unnecessary for the requested parameter calculation.

review.summary: All five examples pass independent mathematical and supplied-source review. All 25 exact assessment locators are mapped and covered. Graph-point calibration uses the same substitution and logarithm method as observation-based calibration; it does not require an additional distinct technique. The examples cover all four nonzero sign combinations. No existing examples or source exceptions require review. Working retains relation-sign alignment without unnecessary phantom equals; prose remains editable and inherits the confirmed blue solution styling. Diagram expressions and annotations are consistent, with annotations confined to solutions. Final-size typography and visual rendering remain for the later capture stage. Accepted assessment mathematics was not re-audited or altered.
